title: CollectionCreateRequest
description: Create a collection bound to a registered embedding model and a chunk strategy. Build-time config is collection identity, so this mints a new collection rather than editing one. The collection is created empty; populate it via POST /v1/ingest with the returned collection id. Omit `id` for a corpus (content-addressed over the build spec, so re-creating the same spec is idempotent); supply `id` for a named library (its own isolated store, even when another library shares the build spec).

embedding.description: Id of a registered model whose task is `embedding` (see GET /v1/admin/models/registry). Its base_urls are SSRF-checked at registration; the model must declare a positive `dim`.

chunk.description: Chunk strategy — part of the collection's build identity, so it is fixed at creation and cannot be edited later. An unknown `method`, or a size/overlap the chosen chunker cannot advance through, is a 400.

method.description: One of fixed, fixed_token, sentence, words, semantic, semantic_pooled (the server's CHUNK_METHODS). Anything else is a 400.

size.description: Chunk budget: characters for fixed/sentence/words, tokens of the collection's embedding model for fixed_token. Must be >= 1 (sentence/words also accept -1 = one chunk per document). Omit for the semantic methods, which derive boundaries from the text — a size sent there would be recorded in the collection's provenance without ever having been used.

overlap.description: Overlap between neighbouring chunks, in the same unit as `size`. Must be >= 0 and strictly less than `size`, otherwise the sliding window never advances. Omit for the semantic methods.

params.description: Free-form extra chunker parameters. The semantic methods read buffer_size (1-50), breakpoint_percentile_threshold (1-100) and min_chunk_length (0-100000); anything omitted falls back to the server default. Unrecognised keys are accepted and stored as-is.

id.description: Optional explicit collection id, naming a *library*. When given, the id is also folded into the physical store name, so two libraries built from the same (model, dim, chunk) spec are isolated from each other rather than aliasing one store. Omitted → both the id and the physical name are derived from the content-addressed (model, dim, chunk) signature.
